recommendation: Test two small companions as one quiet group watching the toolbox work in the deeper workshop area. Keep the moth-only image as the comparison and fallback. Preserve the foreground coding scene and the existing coding/building/resting hierarchy; do not add tree-side play in the first test.
pairRecommendationProposed: Test two small background companions watching the toolbox work as one supporting group; reserve the foreground entirely for Nag's coding scene, keep the moth-only baseline, and remove the cameos if they compete with the coder or obscure the three moth activities at banner size.

placement.zone: Deeper workshop space beside or behind the worktable, away from the foreground bench and the path leading into it. Keep clear of the builder's face, antennae, hammer, hands and toolbox.
placement.action: Both companions attend to the same visible toolbox task. Their eyelines and quiet poses should return attention to the builder rather than create a separate joke or prop interaction.
placement.scaleAndContrast: Start substantially smaller than the workshop moth, with restrained local contrast and the same environmental light. Exact size is a rendering question: do not enlarge a logo merely to make its brand identifiable on a phone.
placement.foreground: No companion, companion prop, logo strip or added text on, beside or overlapping the foreground moth, bench, MacBook or surrounding foreground path.
placement.tree: Leave the resting moth's tree space clear in the first test. A separate playing pair would create another action group and risk taking over the quiet resting beat.

options.judgment: Strongest existing narrative economy and necessary control. The current image already connects coding in front, building behind and resting at the tree. Cameos must add something to that rather than fill apparent empty space.
Preferred bounded test. One small observing group can give the toolbox activity a social audience while keeping it the same activity. This is a plausible benefit, not a demonstrated result.

Higher-risk alternative: one watcher plus two playing by the tree creates two cameo groups and an additional play event. Consider only after the two-companion test proves subordinate at actual banner size; there is no reason to assume the extra group will improve the story.

Do not transfer the full cast into this composition. The reference makes its brightly colored, strongly outlined group the main event. Combining that treatment with three moth appearances and a detailed park is likely to shift the scene toward a product ensemble. This is a compositional prediction; no full-cast variant has been rendered.

failureCriterion: At intended GitHub desktop and narrow banner sizes, the cameo cluster becomes as visually prominent as the foreground coder or MacBook.
The builder's tool-to-box action is obscured, or the three moth activities cease to separate clearly because new figures merge with their silhouettes.
The companions require larger size, brighter color, extra labels or individual props to explain why they are present.
Tree-side play becomes a separate principal event, or a logo lineup replaces the continuous park composition.
Any companion enters the reserved foreground, or the unchanged moth identity/anatomy is altered to accommodate the cast.
